question: Why do we use nursing data integration in the hospital?

options.A: To increase the physical storage space required for paper charts
options.B: To eliminate the need for nurses to record vital signs
options.C: To combine patient information from multiple sources into one clear view
options.D: To reduce the total number of patients admitted to a ward

explanation: You've got this! Data integration simply means bringing scattered patient details together so you can see a complete health record all in one place. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: If a patient's vital signs and drug records are kept in separate systems that don't talk to each other, what is most likely to happen?

options.A: Faster emergency response times during a ward crisis
options.B: Automatic updating of all patient files at the exact same time
options.C: Higher risk of mistakes and scattered care
options.D: Complete elimination of nursing documentation duties

explanation: When systems don't share info, nurses waste time copying things manually, which easily opens the door for errors. Teamwork and shared systems keep our patients safe! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which standard nursing language is specifically used to group and classify the treatments and actions we give to patients?
explanation: Think of NIC as your handy guide that gives a clear, shared name to the actual treatments and nursing actions you perform every day. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why do hospitals love using standardized nursing words in electronic records?

options.A: To make nursing care measurable, visible, and easy to compare everywhere
options.B: To replace doctors' clinical notes with nursing diagnoses
options.C: To slow down how fast nurses document daily care
options.D: To prevent patients from reading their own medical charts

explanation: Standard codes help hospitals track our hard work, show our value as nurses, and compare care quality across different wards and clinics. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: In health tech, what does the word 'interoperability' actually mean?

options.A: Physically networking computers inside a single office
options.B: The ability of different computer systems to talk and share data
options.C: Backing up hospital databases onto external hard drives
options.D: Converting paper medical records into PDF files

explanation: Interoperability is just tech-speak for systems that talk to each other nicely without needing you to re-type everything! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: A clinic gets a new computer system that refuses to read data coming from the lab machine. What is this system missing?
explanation: When separate machines can't share or understand each other's data, they lack interoperability. They need to speak the same digital language! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: What do we call data that truly and correctly matches the real clinical state of a patient?
explanation: Accuracy means what is typed matches reality. Getting the numbers right keeps our clinical decisions safe and sound! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: A nurse types a patient's temperature as 390 degrees instead of 39.0, but the computer blocks it. What safety feature just saved the day?
explanation: Smart software uses validation rules to catch crazy typos before impossible clinical numbers sneak into the official record. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: What feature makes sure hospital staff can only open patient files that match their specific job duties?
explanation: Role-based access keeps patient privacy safe by only opening the doors your specific job requires you to see. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is keeping data secure even more important when hospital computer systems are fully linked together?

options.A: Integrated systems remove the need for nurse passwords
options.B: Patients demand that their medical files be published online
options.C: Computers stop working properly when health data is shared between departments
options.D: Connected networks create more potential entry points for unauthorized people

explanation: The more doors and bridges you build to connect systems, the more careful you have to be about locking them up against snoops! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: How does data integration make your daily life as a nurse easier?

options.A: It automatically cleans the hospital ward rooms
options.B: It cuts down the time you spend hunting for scattered patient info
options.C: It increases the volume of required handwritten paper reports
options.D: It completely removes the need to ever measure vital signs

explanation: No more running around looking for lost folders! Putting everything on one clean screen gives you more time for actual bedside patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)

question: A hospital links lab results straight to the nursing screen and sets up instant phone alerts for danger values. What is the great clinical result?

options.A: Faster spotting and treatment of patients whose health is getting worse
options.B: Less communication between nurses and lab techs
options.C: Higher rates of medicine mix-ups on the ward
options.D: Longer delays in telling doctors about weird lab results

explanation: Quick alerts mean quick action! When our tech flags danger early, we can step in and save lives faster. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)
